To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Higgs mass implies that the fine-tuning in minimal theories of weak scale SUSY is large, and that nondecoupling interactions can increase the HIGGS mass while maintaining natural SUSY.

(1) the Dirac next-to-mininal supersymmetric standard model is the simplest model that simultaneously explains the Higgs bosom mass and the absence of large flavor-changing neutral currents and (2) the Dirac nature of the singlet sector is crucial to maintaining naturalness.

(1) the Higgs mass is naturally enhanced by new singlet states that are not charged under the Standard Model (SM) gauge group, (2) this enhancement occurs even when these singlet states are strongly coupled and receive large soft SUSY breaking masses, and (3) the Higgs phenomenology is modified in ways that are testable at future colliders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question.
the Higgs mass in the MSSM and extensions thereof.
the question of whether there are any new sources of SUS Y breaking that can be consistent with the observed Higgs mass.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Higgs bosons in the minimal supersymmetric standard model are not natural.
the Higgs mass is a natural consequence of supersymmetry, provided one allows for new sources of SUS Y breaking.
the Higgs mass is a very good indicator of the presence of SUSY in the TeV scale.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown a way to have a natural Higgs mass in the MSSM with a Dirac singlet.
the Higgs mass can be naturally enhanced without fine tuning, and that it can be achieved by the nondecoupling effect of a new state.
the Higgs mass in minimal SUSY is natural only with a fine-tuning of about 1% and that this can be improved with nondecoupling, which requires new sources of SUS Y breaking in the singlets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Higgs mass in SUSY is not necessarily a sign of fine-tuning, even if the new states are not very heavy.
the Higgs mass is not a reliable probe of SUSY-breaking effects in theories with new states that can interact with the Higg boson.
nondecoupling Higgs mass contributions can arise from a new sector with large amounts of SUSY breaking, and that the presence of a Dirac mass is essential to maintaining naturalness.
